title: fix: bound detailed usage reads and reuse unchanged reports
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Detailed session-usage reads combine requested session/month ranges with OR. When SQLite statistics still describe a small cache, the planner can scan the full cache table instead of reading the requested partitions. Separately, a completed detail report expires after 30 seconds even when its revision is unchanged, starting another inventory and rollup read behind the returned cached response.

## User Impact

Requested session/month reads stay indexed, and unchanged detailed dashboard polls reuse their completed snapshot. Totals, owner attribution, visibility, incomplete-result retries, byte-budget ordering, and cache eviction remain unchanged. No schema, index, or configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The partition owner now combines independently indexed ranges with UNION ALL and retains the global key order and existing batch size. It shares the existing index-hint expression with the writer. The existing result-cache owner uses revision-based reuse for complete detail snapshots, as overview already does. The query/cache change is net zero production lines; two additional parentheses lines keep the existing SQL guard annotation attached to its expression. There is no new cache.

## Evidence

Two regressions fail on the parent: the real worker's requested-month lookup chooses SCAN cache_entries with sparse statistics, and the real-handler attribution case invokes a usage worker after an unchanged 31-second poll. Both pass with the fix. The expanded focused run passes 39 tests covering attribution, partitions, worker I/O, and worker snapshots; the earlier cache/attribution run passed 35 tests. Independent Codex autoreview reports no actionable P0–P2 findings. `pnpm check:changed --base bd9166435e98460dee2f6bfa53c301ca1ff96a98` passes. CI caught an annotation-placement guard violation, fixed without changing query behavior; the targeted SQL guard, lint and formatting pass after that correction. No Control UI imports of either changed production module were found.

Real Gateway WebSocket measurements use a synthetic 35.3 GiB database, 5,000 sessions, six months of usage, and 62,000 workspace files. Five stable samples per arm, serial A1/B/A2 controls; all full-response digests match per window, with independent expected totals of 1,250,000 tokens and cost 10.

| Measurement | Baseline A1 / A2 | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Linux uncached warm RPC median | 8.03 / 8.34 s | 1.10 s |
| Linux uncached cold-file-eviction RPC median | 8.58 / 8.33 s | 1.55 s |
| Linux cold usage-worker CPU median | 7.95 / 7.69 s | 0.936 s |
| Linux cold usage-reader physical bytes | 79.9 / 79.9 MB | 81.3 MB |
| Unchanged 31-second poll, settled work median | 10.80 / 10.37 s | 41 ms |
| Unchanged poll, total CPU median | 11.85 / 11.32 s | 49 ms |
| Unchanged poll, sampled allocated bytes | 534.7 / 532.8 MB | 32.3 MB |
| Unchanged poll, usage-owner calls / worker CPU | positive / 10.43–10.02 s | 0 / 0 |

The uncached improvement is primarily less scan CPU; physical bytes for this all-session window are essentially unchanged. The revision cache eliminates repeat usage reads. The existing in-memory visibility/response assembly remains linear; this is constant storage work, not a claim that the entire RPC is O(1).

Linux uses Node 24.22.1, 8 CPUs, 16 GiB and ext4, with real Gateway background integrity verification and transcript-facts maintenance active. Cold means owned-file page eviction; retained SQLite pages may stay warm. Usage-reader bytes exclude unrelated background probes. Allocation runs are separate on macOS/Node 26.12.1; an initial run overlapping crash-recovery verification was excluded and replaced with clean A1/B/A2 controls. The long initial incomplete-report convergence loop exhibited heap growth and hit the local default heap limit; preparation resumed from durable rollups in a fresh isolated Gateway. That preparation failure is retained as an unassigned follow-up, not counted as passing measurement proof. No production data was used. These results do not establish sole causation of a production tail without its request parameters and planner state.

Final-head ClawSweeper review has zero open items. CI's patch-caused SQL annotation guard failure was repaired. Both diagnosed setup timeouts passed individual retries through the protected job-rerun API. Completed exact-head CI attempt 3 has only the two inherited release typecheck failures and their aggregate gate; security passed. The remaining release-tooling type errors reproduce at all 21 diagnostic locations on CI's exact main parent `dbc1aa04e88f531910d70512009c74e355311c92` (tested merge `ded9338b7d84fa32732f3d0f980b2961ab80a2d1`): `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json`. Main regression #201802 (`1579eb4dea9ab`) added three required evidence-client methods without updating the existing typed test clients. That failure remains explicitly failed. Landing uses the documented pinned-head inherited-failure exception with exact-parent reproduction and introducer evidence; no unattributed, infrastructure, security, or review failure is waived.
